entity.description: One Darpan error card posted for a check (or an automation with no check) on a run day. The row is the day's dedupe key and the streak's memory: a second failure the same day posts nothing.

field.name: subjectKey
field.description: The check id, or the automation id when the run has no check.

field.name: runDay
field.description: The scheduled date in the automation's own zone.

field.name: triggerType
field.description: "scheduled", or "manual"/"play": a hand-started run has its own slot and never counts toward a streak. "client": the automation's one client "did not run" line that day (no card).

entity.description: ERROR log lines of the whole instance, one row per fingerprint per UTC day, counts added by each flush (darpan.ops.ErrorLogCapture.flush, every 5 minutes). Read by the daily error email. Instance-wide: tenantId is the thread's tenant when the line was first seen, a plain value.

field.name: fingerprint
field.description: Logger plus the message with numbers and ids masked; "OVERFLOW" for lines past the 500-fingerprint cap of one flush window.

field.name: logDay
field.description: UTC day of the aggregate's last line.

field.name: sampleMessage
field.description: The first line's message, up to 255 characters.

field.name: sampleStack
field.description: The first line's stack and causes, up to 4000 characters.

entity.description: The daily Darpan error email (darpan.ops.ErrorDigestSupport): one row per UTC day, created before anything is read or sent (the claim), so two nodes or two job threads send it once. The next email covers everything since the latest row's sentDate.

field.name: digestDay
field.description: The UTC day of the send.

field.name: sentDate
field.description: The end of the window the email covered (the claim's moment). Cleared when no email went out (no address, or the send failed), so the next email covers this day again.
